description: Fork, remove, reactivate and migrate the retained history (memory) of one region, and compare reachability, discrimination, intervention response, generation and later configuration.
question: Does removing a region's retained history change what happens next, and does restoring it re-enter (re-addressed and acted on) with a downstream difference?
manipulated: history operation on region '1' at step 150: none / remove / remove then re-add at step 200 / move to region '4'
fixed: probe intervention (threshold ×1.3 on region '6' at step 220)
measured: paired differences against the intact branch per metric, with a noise branch (other random stream) as control; HRGI-style verdict only when all four re-entry criteria are measured
does_not_show: That history re-entry is general: one region, one window, one world; the runtime is chaotic, so small perturbations diverge — compare every effect with the noise branch.
